\[
g = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \alpha \, \lvert \nabla (G_\sigma * Y) \rvert}},
\qquad
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = g \, \lvert \nabla u \rvert \left(\operatorname{div}\frac{\nabla u}{\lvert \nabla u \rvert} + \nu\right) + \nabla g \cdot \nabla u
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(u\): The inside of the contour, 1 or 0
- \(g\): The edge stopping image
- \(\nu\): The balloon force
- \(\alpha\): The steepness of g
- \(G_\sigma\): A Gaussian of sigma

u is 1 inside the contour and 0 outside, and starts as the selection. The image g is near 1 in flat areas and near 0 on edges. The equation is the geodesic active contour of Caselles, Kimmel and Sapiro. Marquez-Neila, Baumela and Alvarez replaced each of its terms with a morphological step. The balloon force nu becomes a dilation or erosion by one pixel. It acts only where g is above a threshold divided by the size of nu. The scikit-image code sets the threshold to the 40th percentile of g. The term grad g dot grad u pulls the contour into the valleys of g, the edges. The curvature term becomes a smoothing with the operators SI and IS, run the given number of times. Every step only switches pixels between 0 and 1, so there is no step size to choose.
